jobs.title: Field Technician
jobs.description:
Astro Pak
is the nation's leading precision cleaning and passivation contractor specializing in on-site cleaning of high purity gas and fluid systems, as well as precision cleaning of components and hardware at the company’s Cleanroom facilities. Astro Pak
provides services to over 15 sectors including: Data Centers, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical, Aerospace, Semiconductor, and other selected Industrial markets. The company, founded in 1959, has performed on-site precision chemical cleaning in every State of the Union as well as several projects in Asia, Canada, continental Europe, England, Ireland and Mexico.

Astro Pak is looking for motivated individuals who want more than a typical job. As an Associate Field Technician
, you’ll travel to cutting-edge facilities across the country while learning a specialized technical trade used in industries like aerospace, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, and advanced manufacturing.

If you enjoy hands-on work, solving problems, and seeing new places while building valuable technical skills, this role could be a great fit.

$3,000 Sign-On Bonus********

What You’ll Experience

This is not a typical entry-level job. It’s a traveling technical career path
.

You’ll receive immersive training and work alongside experienced technicians performing specialized chemical cleaning and passivation on mission-critical fluid and gas systems.

Every project is different. One week you may be working at a semiconductor facility, the next supporting aerospace manufacturing.

Expect

Extensive travel to project sites across the U.S.
Hands-on work with specialized equipment and chemical processes
Rapid skill development and certifications
Opportunities to grow into senior technician or leadership roles

Travel Requirements

80%+ travel nationwide
30–50% night shift work
Overtime, weekends, holidays, and short-notice travel may be required

What You’ll Do

As part of a field service team, you will:

Set up and operate specialized equipment for chemical cleaning and passivation
Safely handle process chemicals such as citric acid and caustics
Use PPE and follow strict safety and compliance procedures
Load, transport, and unload project equipment and materials
Drive company vehicles to job sites (vans, trucks, forklifts)
Perform hands-on work in a variety of environments (indoors, outdoors, rooftops)
Maintain organized workspaces aligned with 5S/CEO standards
Complete OSHA and internal safety training
Support mission-critical customer facilities across the country

Who Thrives In This Role

We hire for attitude and train for success.

The Best Candidates Are

Mechanically inclined
Comfortable working with tools and equipment
Adaptable to new environments
Safety-focused
Excited about travel and hands-on work
Interested in building a long-term technical career

Basic Requirements

Valid Class C driver’s license with clean driving record
Real ID or Passport required for air travel
Ability to attend two weeks of paid training in California within the first 3 weeks of employment
Medical DOT certificate
Strong math skills (ratios, percentages)
Comfortable using mobile technology and basic programs (Word, Excel, Outlook)
Fluent in English with strong communication skills
Ability to lift 50 lbs. and work in PPE in changing environments
Willingness to work night shifts, overtime, weekends, and holidays

Preferred (But Not Required)

High School Diploma or GED
Technical schooling or trade certification
OSHA / HAZWOPER / Confined Space certifications
Field service or hazardous chemical handling experience

Why Join Astro Pak?

Paid Training & Certifications

No experience required. We provide hands-on training and help you earn industry certifications.

Travel Opportunities

Work at advanced manufacturing and technology facilities across the country while building your career.

Career Growth

Many of our technicians advance quickly into senior technical roles, trainers, or leadership positions.

Team Culture

Work alongside experienced professionals in a safety-first, supportive team environment.

Competitive Benefits

Highly subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid time off and family leave
Travel stipend
Training and development opportunities
Flexible spending accounts and more

Compensation:
The pay for this position typically has a starting rate of $20-$21. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience and location

jobs.title: Staff Environmental Scientist 1
jobs.description:
Find your path and enjoy the journey at Haley & Aldrich
. With us, you’ll tackle clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments – and, in turn, build stronger communities. You’ll work with teams of passionate colleagues, driven by a commitment to technical excellence and continuous learning.

As a company, we aim to build a world where communities go beyond resilience, embracing change as an opportunity to enhance safety, well-being, and quality of life. Join us to accelerate this vision and your professional development.

We are looking to add new talent to our growing team! We are currently seeking a Staff Environmental Scientist 1, Stormwater
to work in a technical support role with highly skilled professionals on diverse project teams in a dynamic environment. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing group and company and get involved in a variety of projects for a diverse range of clients.

This position offers a recent graduate the opportunity to support stormwater quality management and environmental compliance projects. During the stormwater season, generally October through April, the selected candidate will work primarily in the field at project sites in Ventura/Los Angeles Counties. Responsibilities will include stormwater sampling, compliance inspections, coordination with contractors and laboratories, implementation of standard operating procedures, data management, and technical reporting. Rain-event response will require early-morning starts and on-call availability, including some weekends and potentially holidays. Outside the stormwater season, the position will generally be divided between other field assignments and office-based data analysis and reporting. Due to site-specific permit requirements, the selected candidate must be able to report to the designated primary project site within one hour when required. Relocation assistance is available, if needed. This is a full-time
position in the Los Angeles/Ventura County Area assigned virtually to our Costa Mesa, CA office.

Duties/Responsibilities

In this position, you will:

Conduct field investigations and assessments of soil, groundwater, surface water, etc. using approved industry standard procedures.
Conduct basic construction observation, including quality control documentation and field testing tasks.
Conduct or oversee remedial system O&M and field pilot study demonstrations.
Prepare and maintain accurate and detailed documentation of activities both in the field and during data evaluation.
Apply academic training and use computer software to perform calculations and evaluation of information.
Support project environmental data reduction and summarization.
Support project feasibility study, remedial design, cost estimating, and permitting tasks.
Assist with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS tasks.
Draft technical sections of project communications and reports.
Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimating for proposal efforts on small- to medium-sized project opportunities.
Perform all work in accordance with company and client health and safety protocols.
Demonstrate the company’s foundational safety behaviors.
Support site-specific environmental compliance activities related to stormwater quality management, construction and post-construction best management practices, NPDES permitting, and California stormwater requirements.
Conduct stormwater sampling, site inspections, and field monitoring activities in accordance with applicable permits, project plans, and standard operating procedures.
Coordinate field activities with project team members, contractors, laboratories, and other project stakeholders.
Assist with permit reviews and the evaluation of applicable local, regional, state, and federal stormwater requirements.
Support stormwater data validation, analysis, visualization, and preparation of compliance reports and other technical deliverables.
Support field programs involving stormwater quality management, contaminated-site investigation and management, and environmental protection-related construction, maintenance, and monitoring.

Skills/Experience

Minimum Skills and Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Water Resources Engineering, Geology, Civil Engineering, or related field.
0 to 2 years of related field experience.
Proficient technical writing, verbal communication, reasoning, and time management skills.
Able to work independently or with minimal direction in performing tasks and assignments under the direction of senior staff.
Desire to learn and grow in your profession, demonstrate a positive attitude, strong work ethic, resourcefulness, flexibility, and ownership.
Familiar with environmental analytical testing and data reduction techniques for soil, water, and air.
Able to meet the physical requirements of the position: lift 50 lbs., traverse unstable/sloping sites and landscapes, work outside in a range of weather conditions, and have the stamina for moderate physical activity for the majority of field working hours.
Able to travel to work locations that may require overnight stays.
Able to work primarily in the field during the stormwater season, generally October through April, including early-morning starts and on-call response during rain events, weekends, and holidays when required.
Able to report to the designated primary project site in Los Angeles/Ventura County area within one hour due to site-specific stormwater permit requirements.
Able to pass client-specific background screenings and obtain required site access badges.
Able to handle large sample volumes and safely operate or ride in field vehicles, including four-wheel-drive vehicles when necessary.
Must have reliable transportation or be able to rent a vehicle for site access; primary project sites are not accessible by public transportation.

Preferred Skills

Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Water Resources Engineering or related field.
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER training.
Interest in obtaining one or more construction stormwater certifications, such as CISEC, CPESC, CPSWQ, or CESSWI.
Experience or academic exposure related to Industrial NPDES, Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System, or MS4 programs.
Experience with soil, groundwater, air, or stormwater sampling and reporting methods.
Familiarity with California stormwater regulations, construction and post-construction best management practices, and environmental compliance inspections.

The salary range for this position in Costa Mesa, CA and Los Angeles, CA
is $75,000 - $85,000 annually
. Actual compensation will be based upon a variety of factors such as education, related work experience, certificates, skills, and current market conditions. Haley & Aldrich reviews salary ranges each quarter to assess competitiveness with the market.

About Haley & Aldrich

Haley & Aldrich is committed to solving our clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments. Our team of 1,000+ engineers and scientists across the United States draws inspiration from one mission: to work closely with clients as they navigate change to create safer, more robust places to live and work. Since our founding in 1957, organizations across the public and private sectors have relied on us for technical excellence and empathetic leadership that achieve results and secure a thriving tomorrow. Find us at haleyaldrich.com and LinkedIn .

Haley & Aldrich is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, race, age, disability, veteran, or any other legally protected status. We offer excellent career growth, a highly competitive total compensation plan, and a solid benefits package. Interested candidates should apply on our Careers page.

Summary

Spire is seeking an Environmental Engineer or Scientist II to work in Alabama. This position will be responsible for performing field inspections, permitting, waste disposal and remediation to support Spire's pipeline work and ongoing operation of natural gas facilities.

Company Overview

We are committed to understanding the needs of the homes and businesses we serve. That's why we're always looking for driven, collaborative people to join our team. Because we believe that offering our customers the best service means bringing together the best people.

And we find the best by hiring those who share our values of safety, inclusion and integrity, and demonstrate the competencies that bring the Spire vision, mission and culture to life:

Adaptability: We embrace change, continuously seeking opportunities for improvement while remaining open-minded and flexible in response to evolving conditions and customer, stakeholder and company needs.
Collaboration: We achieve more together through a foundation of respect, embracing healthy conflict, actively seeking and providing actionable feedback and fostering an environment where everyone’s input is welcomed.
Ownership: We see things through, demonstrate accountability, honor commitments, take responsibility for outcomes and demonstrate initiative.

By living our values and competencies, we strive to create an environment where employees feel welcome, respected and valued.

Duties and Responsibilities

Inspect Company facilities and projects for compliance with environmental and related regulations; provide recommendations for needed corrective or preventive actions.
Perform reviews of projects flagged by Construction Engineering for environmental issues. Train Construction Engineering on environmental review processes.
Secure environmental permits and completely required regulatory submittals, especially USACE permits, permits requiring special certifications, and permits with longer timelines.
Oversee consultants performing permitting functions.
Manage and arrange disposal of new regulated waste generated by the Company.
Manage and/or conduct evaluation and remediation of former manufactured gas plant sites and odorant, petroleum or other remediation and risk mitigation sites.
Track and prepare air permitting submittals.
Oversee air permitting performed by consultants.
Maintain knowledge of applicable environmental regulations.
Read and interpret applicable environmental regulations, especially state environmental agencies, EPA and OSHA regulations having direct and/or potential impact on Company operations.
Assist in preparing regulatory documentation and responses to environmental field incidents and employee questions or requests.
Assist with regulated greenhouse gas data collection and reporting.
Manage environmental projects. This includes bid proposal preparation, scheduling, oversight and budget tracking.
Assist in developing and conducting environmental training.

Essential Characteristics

Demonstrates a strong customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering exceptional service and support.
Collaborates effectively in a team environment while fostering positive working relationships across diverse groups.
Communicates clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing.
Takes initiative, demonstrates accountability, and consistently delivers high-quality results.
Analyzes issues, troubleshoots problems, and develops practical solutions.
Adapts effectively to changing priorities, business needs, and work environments.
Shows a commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and career growth.
Maintains the highest standards of ethics, integrity, and professionalism.
Promotes and supports a safe, healthy, and compliant work environment.
Manages multiple priorities effectively while working independently and meeting deadlines.
Values diversity, equity, and inclusion, recognizing and respecting the unique perspectives and contributions of others.
Builds trust and rapport with individuals from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences.
Demonstrates strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.

Required Education (certifications, licenses)

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, environmental science, or similar technical degree, required.
Industry certifications - EIT, GRIT, CEP, CHMM, preferred.

Required Knowledge, Skill And Abilities

Minimum 2-3 years’ professional experience, required.
General utility knowledge is preferred.
Knowledge of permitting and regulatory environment required (Alabama or Missouri only).
Strong knowledge of local, state and federal environmental regulations and permitting processes.

Physical demands, environment and schedule

Shared office environment and field (Ongoing exposure to the elements and rough off-road terrain may occur.)
Typically, 7:30 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.
Scheduled, periodic on-call duties for incident evaluation and response, as rotated through the department.
Overtime and/or travel will occasionally be required.

new_jobs.description:
Find your path and enjoy the journey at Haley & Aldrich
. With us, you’ll tackle clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments – and, in turn, build stronger communities. You’ll work with teams of passionate colleagues, driven by a commitment to technical excellence and continuous learning.

As a company, we aim to build a world where communities go beyond resilience, embracing change as an opportunity to enhance safety, well-being, and quality of life. Join us to accelerate this vision and your professional development.

We are looking to add new talent to our growing team! We are currently seeking a Staff Environmental Scientist 1, Stormwater
to work in a technical support role with highly skilled professionals on diverse project teams in a dynamic environment. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing group and company and get involved in a variety of projects for a diverse range of clients.

This position offers a recent graduate the opportunity to support stormwater quality management and environmental compliance projects. During the stormwater season, generally October through April, the selected candidate will work primarily in the field at project sites in Ventura/Los Angeles Counties. Responsibilities will include stormwater sampling, compliance inspections, coordination with contractors and laboratories, implementation of standard operating procedures, data management, and technical reporting. Rain-event response will require early-morning starts and on-call availability, including some weekends and potentially holidays. Outside the stormwater season, the position will generally be divided between other field assignments and office-based data analysis and reporting. Due to site-specific permit requirements, the selected candidate must be able to report to the designated primary project site within one hour when required. Relocation assistance is available, if needed. This is a full-time
position in the Los Angeles/Ventura County Area assigned virtually to our Costa Mesa, CA office.

Duties/Responsibilities

In this position, you will:

Conduct field investigations and assessments of soil, groundwater, surface water, etc. using approved industry standard procedures.
Conduct basic construction observation, including quality control documentation and field testing tasks.
Conduct or oversee remedial system O&M and field pilot study demonstrations.
Prepare and maintain accurate and detailed documentation of activities both in the field and during data evaluation.
Apply academic training and use computer software to perform calculations and evaluation of information.
Support project environmental data reduction and summarization.
Support project feasibility study, remedial design, cost estimating, and permitting tasks.
Assist with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS tasks.
Draft technical sections of project communications and reports.
Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimating for proposal efforts on small- to medium-sized project opportunities.
Perform all work in accordance with company and client health and safety protocols.
Demonstrate the company’s foundational safety behaviors.
Support site-specific environmental compliance activities related to stormwater quality management, construction and post-construction best management practices, NPDES permitting, and California stormwater requirements.
Conduct stormwater sampling, site inspections, and field monitoring activities in accordance with applicable permits, project plans, and standard operating procedures.
Coordinate field activities with project team members, contractors, laboratories, and other project stakeholders.
Assist with permit reviews and the evaluation of applicable local, regional, state, and federal stormwater requirements.
Support stormwater data validation, analysis, visualization, and preparation of compliance reports and other technical deliverables.
Support field programs involving stormwater quality management, contaminated-site investigation and management, and environmental protection-related construction, maintenance, and monitoring.

Skills/Experience

Minimum Skills and Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Water Resources Engineering, Geology, Civil Engineering, or related field.
0 to 2 years of related field experience.
Proficient technical writing, verbal communication, reasoning, and time management skills.
Able to work independently or with minimal direction in performing tasks and assignments under the direction of senior staff.
Desire to learn and grow in your profession, demonstrate a positive attitude, strong work ethic, resourcefulness, flexibility, and ownership.
Familiar with environmental analytical testing and data reduction techniques for soil, water, and air.
Able to meet the physical requirements of the position: lift 50 lbs., traverse unstable/sloping sites and landscapes, work outside in a range of weather conditions, and have the stamina for moderate physical activity for the majority of field working hours.
Able to travel to work locations that may require overnight stays.
Able to work primarily in the field during the stormwater season, generally October through April, including early-morning starts and on-call response during rain events, weekends, and holidays when required.
Able to report to the designated primary project site in Los Angeles/Ventura County area within one hour due to site-specific stormwater permit requirements.
Able to pass client-specific background screenings and obtain required site access badges.
Able to handle large sample volumes and safely operate or ride in field vehicles, including four-wheel-drive vehicles when necessary.
Must have reliable transportation or be able to rent a vehicle for site access; primary project sites are not accessible by public transportation.

Preferred Skills

Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Water Resources Engineering or related field.
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, and GIS.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER training.
Interest in obtaining one or more construction stormwater certifications, such as CISEC, CPESC, CPSWQ, or CESSWI.
Experience or academic exposure related to Industrial NPDES, Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System, or MS4 programs.
Experience with soil, groundwater, air, or stormwater sampling and reporting methods.
Familiarity with California stormwater regulations, construction and post-construction best management practices, and environmental compliance inspections.

The salary range for this position in Costa Mesa, CA and Los Angeles, CA
is $75,000 - $85,000 annually
. Actual compensation will be based upon a variety of factors such as education, related work experience, certificates, skills, and current market conditions. Haley & Aldrich reviews salary ranges each quarter to assess competitiveness with the market.

Haley & Aldrich is committed to solving our clients’ most meaningful challenges in the built and natural environments. Our team of 1,000+ engineers and scientists across the United States draws inspiration from one mission: to work closely with clients as they navigate change to create safer, more robust places to live and work. Since our founding in 1957, organizations across the public and private sectors have relied on us for technical excellence and empathetic leadership that achieve results and secure a thriving tomorrow.
